A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mechanistic CLIP defense, renamed Dyslexify in v2. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results, linear-probe experiments, circuit interventions, and appendix analyses of intrinsic dimensionality and attention sinks.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original experiments and adds medical evaluations, OCR results, runtime measurements and comparisons with image blurring.

M1.justification: v1 Algorithm 1 adds ranked heads until clean accuracy breaches its tolerance. v2 additionally requires each ablation to improve typographic accuracy, skips unsuccessful candidates, and stops after a consecutive-skip limit. This substantially changes circuit selection, while retaining CLS-only head ablation.

E1.justification: v2 adds typographic Food-101 and Aircraft evaluations, IIIT5K word recognition, and medical skin-lesion classification with clean and attacked inputs, including ISIC2019, HAM10k and BCN20k. The original general-vision and real typographic-attack benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Defense-Prefix and unmodified-model comparisons are retained. v2 Appendix J adds an evaluated PaddleOCR-plus-Gaussian-blur defense and its combination with Dyslexify across five model sizes, substantially expanding the defense comparison.

E3.justification: Circuit construction changes from v1's class-balanced 5% ImageNet-100 training subset to the full training split, with an additional typographic accuracy criterion and k=10 skip limit. New protocols include IIIT5K small/medium-lexicon classification and runtime comparisons on an H200 using matched pipelines and batch sizes.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of OCR capability loss, runtime and memory costs, medical-model probes, and combined blurring/circuit interventions. Circuit-ablation curves are revised and extended to WhyLesionCLIP. The original PCA and attention-sink studies remain, rather than being new appendix additions.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Existing graphical error bars receive no new uncertainty explanation. The new mean-plus-two-standard-deviations head-score cutoff is an analysis threshold, not a repeated-run uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Many scores, circuit sizes and plotted results change. For example, ViT-L RTA-100 accuracy changes from 61.60% to 71.00%; the Defense-Prefix ranking reverses on RTA-100 and PAINT, while clean Food-101 now favors Defense-Prefix. New medical, OCR, runtime and blurring results appear. Construction settings and base-model scores also change, preventing attribution to an isolated same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The written attention-score definition changes substantively: v1 Equation 6 divides each attention entry by itself, whereas v2 Equation 7 divides summed typographic attention by summed spatial attention. This corrects the formula's attention dependence. The PCA definition and attention-intervention equation remain; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v2 adds medical-model protection as an explicit contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. Its headline ImageNet-100-Typo accuracy gain changes from 19.6 to 22.06 percentage points. The central claim of defending CLIP through causal head interventions without fine-tuning remains.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses OCR unsuitability, trade-offs against the stronger blurring baseline, and possible effects of training-data typography on medical models. It also newly asserts that non-differentiability prevents adaptive-attack evaluation. The existing spatial-token limitation remains. Figure 10's medical-probe interpretation conflicts with its plotted ordering.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit project/code links, a reproducibility statement, attack fonts, a two-token-row attention mask description, and precise blurring settings (kernel 51, sigma 25). It documents H200 timing conditions and Titan RTX memory feasibility. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that interventions use Prisma is removed.

R1.justification: The main related-work argument is largely retained. v2 adds references supporting medical datasets, IIIT5K, PaddleOCR/OpenCV and adaptive-attack evaluation, while removing Prisma and several broad VLM/generative-model references. Appendix J additionally positions mechanistic intervention relative to image-level preprocessing.

P1.justification: v2 renames the paper and method, shifts terminology from training-free to gradient-free, and edits explanatory prose. It reframes probing as motivation, redistributes the standalone dataset section, folds Discussion into Conclusion, and adds backmatter and appendix contents. Much of the existing exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the head-score/probe figures using thresholded masks and different axis arrangements, redistributes ablation plots, and moves the circuit-size table into the appendix. New medical figures and OCR, runtime and blurring tables materially expand the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves assessment of the defense's practical value: Appendices H–J quantify OCR losses, computational costs, and a stronger blurring alternative, addressing important gaps in v1's robustness–utility evidence. Medical experiments, the corrected score formula and explicit implementation/access information further strengthen the paper. New reporting problems remain, particularly Figure 10's reversed interpretation and the unsupported dismissal of adaptive evaluation, but these do not outweigh the substantial gains in comparative evidence and transparency.
